name: com.unity.netcode.gameobjects
description: Netcode for GameObjects is a high-level netcode SDK that provides networking capabilities to GameObject/MonoBehaviour workflows within Unity and sits on top of underlying transport layer.

samples.description: A lightweight sample to get started

_upm.changelog:
### Fixed

- Issue where `NetworkAnimator` logged an error for a trigger-conditioned transition into an Exit node, and a client that joined during that transition, or during one into a sub-state machine, did not synchronize with it. Transitions that pass through Exit, Entry or sub-state machine nodes now resolve to the state they reach, and a late-joining client cross-fades from the matching originating state when several states transition into the same destination. (#4240)
- Fixed a NullReferenceException that would be thrown if a MonoBehaviour derived from NetworkManager defines it's own Awake or OnEnable. (#4237)
- Issue where `NetworkTime` reported a `TickOffset` of almost a whole tick, instead of zero, for some times that land on a tick (for example 0.3 at a tick rate of 10), which put `TickWithPartial` one tick ahead or, in long sessions, `Tick` one tick behind. Times between minus one tick and zero now report tick -1 with a positive `TickOffset`, as other negative times do. (#4227)
- Issue where bits written with `BitWriter` were lost when a later `BitWriter.TryBeginWriteBits` call in the same bitwise context grew the `FastBufferWriter`. The bytes written earlier in that context were replaced with zeros or uninitialized memory. (#4225)
- Issue where a growable `FastBufferWriter` created with a size of 0 never returned from its first write or `TryBeginWrite` call that needed the buffer to grow. (#4223)
- Issue where a `FastBufferReader` created with an offset and the default length of -1 read past the end of its source. The `ArraySegment<byte>` overload that takes an offset now applies it from the start of the segment. (#4221)
- Issue where a client promoted to session owner could throw an exception when synchronizing a newly joining client. (#4217)
- Issue where a client synchronized while a `NetworkList<T>` still had unsent changes applied those changes twice, resulting in duplicate entries and index-based events landing on the wrong elements on that client. (#4215)
- Issue where showing a `NetworkObject` with `NetworkShow` while its `NetworkVariable` updates were held back by `NetworkVariableUpdateTraits` stopped those pending changes from being sent until the variable was modified again. (#4215)
- Issue where a rejected parent change, for example one made by a client without parenting authority, restored the `NetworkObject`'s parent but left it at the moved position when the change was made with `worldPositionStays` disabled. The original position, rotation and scale are now restored. (#4203)
- Issue where moving a `NetworkObject` into another scene made the clients that did not observe it log "Trying to synchronize NetworkObjectId but it was not spawned". The scene migration is now only sent to the clients that observe the `NetworkObject`. (#4185)
- Issue where a `NetworkObject` that was moved into another scene while hidden from a client spawned in that client's active scene when it was shown with `NetworkShow`, instead of the scene it is in on the server. (#4185)
- Issue where mixed authority nested `NetworkTransform` instances could stop child/nested instances from updating because an authoritative `NetworkTransform` (root or otherwise) would remove the `NetworkObject` from the update group, preventing non-authoritative instances from updating their state on the authority side. (#4169)
